questions.answer_plain: Adding carbon-monoxide-eating microbes at one percent of the soil community changes carbon monoxide uptake over two weeks by 0.5 % (range 0.5 to 0.6 %), and adding five percent changes uptake by 2.7 % (range 2.7 to 3.1 %), where carbon-monoxide eaters are already present, so uptake goes up in every case we tried. In a soil community that starts with no carbon-monoxide eaters at all, adding a carrier strain switches uptake from none to some, whereas adding a microbe without the carbon-monoxide genes leaves uptake at none.

questions.answer_plain: Doubling hydrogen in the air increases soil hydrogen uptake over two weeks by 100 % (range 100 to 100 %), and tenfold air hydrogen increases uptake by 900 %, so uptake goes up in every case we tried. Because soil uptake in the twin is directly proportional to the hydrogen level in the air, percentage uptake rises in lockstep with air concentration.
